feedback: Implementation is correct, in-scope, and all four hard gates are green; AC-F01..F06 are substantively met. To push quality higher in a follow-up: (1) Add an end-to-end executor/migrate test that drives a real char-limit/empty-required product through makePerItemExecutor in dryRun and asserts status==='requires_manual' (currently AC-F04's surfacing is only tested on validateEditItemParams in isolation, not through plan/executor). (2) Because buildYahooEditItemParams always pre-trims before validateEditItemParams runs, the length-violation branch of validateYahooFieldLimits can never fire on the normal flow (fitFullWidth guarantees <=max) — it only ever surfaces empty-required; document this as a defensive double-check or add a test proving the empty-required path drives requires_manual. (3) caption (html:true=false, HTML-allowed, max 5000) is truncated by raw code-point fit, which can cut mid-HTML-tag producing malformed markup for >5000 full-width captions; consider tag-aware truncation or stripping trailing broken tags. (4) Half-width detection treats Latin-1/accented/full-width-form chars (0x80-0xFF, 0xFF00-0xFF60) as full=1 (safe/conservative, never exceeds Yahoo's count but may over-trim names containing accents/symbols) — acceptable, but note it in the table comment. (5) Truncation is a hard head-cut with no word/space-boundary or ellipsis handling (task's 'preserve meaning where possible' is only minimally honored); fine for Japanese but consider trimming at the last space for half-width-heavy fields. (6) validateEditItemParams.missing now mixes field-name tokens (e.g. 'path') with human messages (e.g. 'path カテゴリ名「…」が全角20を超過'); callers matching exact field names won't match message strings — consider a structured {field,reason} shape behind the back-compat array.
risks: validateEditItemParams length-check is effectively unreachable for over-length on the normal flow because buildYahooEditItemParams always pre-trims; only empty-required cases actually surface as requires_manual in dry-run
caption (HTML-allowed, 5000) raw code-point truncation can split an HTML tag for very long captions, yielding malformed markup
Conservative half-width rule counts accented Latin / full-width-form / Latin-1 chars as full=1, which over-trims (never exceeds) such fields
AC-F04 surfacing is only unit-tested on validateEditItemParams in isolation; no test exercises the plan/executor dry-run path with a char-limit/empty-required product
Truncation is non-word-boundary head-cut; meaning preservation is minimal (acceptable for Japanese-dominant fields)
recommended_next_changes: Add executor/migrate dry-run test: feed an empty-path (or category-unresolved) product and assert status==='requires_manual' with no write deps invoked (end-to-end AC-F04)
Make caption/HTML-allowed truncation tag-aware (or strip a trailing partial tag) to avoid malformed markup at the 5000 boundary
Add a test asserting that after fitYahooFieldLimits the validateYahooFieldLimits length branch never reports over-length (documents the defensive double-check)
Document in YAHOO_FIELD_LIMITS comment that non-ASCII non-half-kana code points count as full=1 (conservative), and consider word/space-boundary trimming for half-width-heavy fields
Consider returning structured {field,reason} violations behind the back-compat missing[] so callers can match field identity rather than human message strings
